name: Network Attacks & Analysis
tagline: Packet capture, on-path interception, host discovery, and connectivity utilities for understanding and testing traffic on networks you operate.

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.desc: Graphical packet analyzer that decodes hundreds of protocols, follows TCP streams, and reassembles sessions live or from a saved capture.
tools.when: See the actual bytes and protocol conversations behind a traffic sample, or replay an issue from a .pcap taken on a machine you control.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.desc: Command-line packet capture using Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) expressions; the standard for headless logging and scripted sniffing.
tools.when: On servers, routers, or lab hosts where no GUI exists, or when writing a rolling capture to a file for later analysis.

tools.name: tshark
tools.desc: Wireshark's terminal sibling: captures, decrypts, and prints live or offline traffic with the full dissector set and CSV/JSON output.
tools.when: Get Wireshark-grade dissection piped into grep, awk, or analysis scripts without launching a GUI.

tools.name: tcpflow
tools.desc: Reassembles TCP sessions from a capture into separate per-connection files, ignoring lower-level packet noise.
tools.when: Reconstruct actual transferred content (files, HTTP bodies) from a .pcap you own instead of inspecting packets one at a time.

tools.name: bettercap
tools.desc: Modular framework for MITM, ARP/DNS/DHCP spoofing, and credential sniffing with an interactive shell and RESTful API for scripting.
tools.when: On a network you operate, to test which plaintext protocols (HTTP, FTP, telnet) leak over the wire and how clients react to spoofing.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive HTTPS interception proxy with a terminal UI, Python addon scripting, and TLS interception via its own CA you install on your devices.
tools.when: Inspect and rewrite HTTP/HTTPS traffic from an app, device, or CLI you control, with the proxy cert explicitly trusted on that device.

tools.name: responder
tools.desc: Answers LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS name-resolution queries on a subnet and logs or relays credentials passed over those protocols to its own listeners.
tools.when: Test Windows-style authentication flows in a lab and check whether clients will send net-NTLM hashes when their expected resolver goes silent.

tools.name: arp-scan
tools.desc: Sends ARP requests to every address in a subnet and lists live hosts by IP and MAC/OUI vendor; the most reliable way to map a local network.
tools.when: First step when on a network you administer: enumerate every physical host on the LAN, since ARP is answered even where ICMP is filtered.

tools.name: netdiscover
tools.desc: Active and passive ARP-based host discovery with a live-updating table of MAC address, vendor, and IP.
tools.when: Continuous visual recon of a local network, or a quick live view while monitoring the LAN over time.

tools.name: fping
tools.desc: Bulk ICMP pinger that sweeps a range of targets in parallel and prints alive/dead results in a script-friendly stream.
tools.when: Fast liveness check of a large IP range when hosts are off-subnet, where ARP-based discovery cannot reach.

tools.name: socat
tools.desc: Bidirectional relay that forwards, listens on, and connects across TCP, UDP, UNIX sockets, and files; flexible byte plumbing for testing services.
tools.when: Expose a local service through a relay, forward ports between lab hosts, or inject/monitor raw data flows in ad-hoc setups.

tools.name: ncat
tools.desc: Nmap's free, MIT-licensed netcat: connect, listen, and relay TCP/UDP with TLS, proxy modes, and easy scripting built in.
tools.when: Quick read/write tests against a listening port, banner grabbing, or one-shot TCP/UDP checks while debugging connectivity.

tools.name: hping3
tools.desc: Packet-crafting tool that builds custom TCP/UDP/ICMP packets via raw sockets, with control over flags, timing, and fragmentation.
tools.when: Answer questions like "does this firewall actually drop that flagged packet?" by sending hand-crafted probes from a host you control.

tools.name: proxychains
tools.desc: Routes any TCP client through a strict, random, or dynamic chain of HTTP/SOCKS proxies, forcing connections out via chosen exits.
tools.when: Test whether an application can be tunneled through proxies and observe the egress path a tool takes in controlled lab scenarios.

tools.name: dig
tools.desc: The standard DNS query tool from the BIND suite: any record type, MX priority, zone-transfer attempts, and query tracing against a chosen resolver.
tools.when: Resolve names in isolation, verify records against a specific server, or trace how a lookup flows through resolvers in one command.

tools.name: whois
tools.desc: Queries WHOIS/registration databases for domain ownership, registrar, name servers, and IP allocation details.
tools.when: Collect registrant, registrar, and registration dates for a domain, or the owning organization of an IP range, before deeper analysis.
